title: Absurdly useful tip for AI Game Dev - Make a Screen Snipping/Drawing Tool
author: Internal-Capital7471
selftext:
https://preview.redd.it/bfu5rrwa35th1.png?width=1069&format=png&auto=webp&s=6c8ba16223b5467f219eb97e69a9dfd96e4a1cc9

I didn't have a good screen snip/drawing tool and didnt want to buy one, so I prompted Claude to make it -- fast and easy. Now, when I have an issue with my game, i clip it and draw inside of it, then explain with text what I want. It works so, so well. In this screenshot, there's a 2nd floor above this dining area, and I thought it would need a pillar for some realism. In my kitchen minigame area, it was incredibly useful in imagining what the line layout should look like. 

Do yourself a favor, and create a snipping tool if you haven't.

comments.author: Unturned1
comments.body: So, I have been doing screen shots and snipping for awhile, windows does have this built in, what I just realized is that maybe an in game engine tool which let me snip the part of the scene that I want to address, and sends the the nodes / scene / snip / associated information to directly to the CLI along with a comment is actually a faster way to get things done rather than typing information after copy pasting.

comments.author: Melodic-Chemistry127

Good idea, though!

replies.author: Internal-Capital7471
replies.body:
You could go even further. I had an app that I was tired of waiting for builds to see changes, so I made it hot-reload compatible. Then, inside the app, I added a chatbox that logs to a file that I had Claude polling, looking at it. It would read that log, see the messages, respond to them, and hot-reload changes back to the build. I also included a screenshot on the chatbox to attach to messages, but no drawing feature.

It was finicky setting up, but worked well after \~5 or 6 hours of troubleshooting and testing. I dunno if its worth doing quite that much work every project.. my github repo is like 20+ random projects now. Dont think I want to take the time to genericize this, when the clipping tool is working pretty well and fast and is generic. Im not really saving that much time automating and improving that, when that process absolutely is not the bottleneck.

comments.author: Alessioga
comments.body: I created a skill, publicly available on my site - 0n1studios.com in the journal section - that does something similar, just faster: AI will take a series of screenshots of what you want to review or change, it will put them in an artifact in Claude, and you will be able to add literal sticky notes on it: the artifact tracks the position of them and the feedback as decision that you can then submit in one go. It’s called Marginalia, and the code behind it is also download from GitHub if you are interested.
